stories.headline: Business Groups Push for 10-Year CISA Renewal

daily.headline: The Morris worm slows the early internet to a crawl
daily.technical: On this day in 1988, a Cornell student released the Morris worm, which spread across Unix machines by abusing weaknesses in sendmail, finger and weak passwords. A bug made it reinfect machines repeatedly, overloading thousands of computers. It led to the creation of the first CERT team at Carnegie Mellon.
daily.why_it_matters: The first big lesson that one flaw can take down many connected systems.

daily.headline: Check which apps can see your location and photos
daily.technical: Apps often ask for more access than they need. On Android, go to Settings then Privacy to review permissions; on iPhone, Settings then Privacy & Security. Switch off access an app doesn't need, and remove apps you no longer use.
daily.why_it_matters: Less access means less to leak if an app is compromised.

daily.headline: Norsk Hydro hit by LockerGoga ransomware
daily.technical: Seven years ago, aluminium maker Norsk Hydro was hit by LockerGoga ransomware, forcing some plants to switch to manual operations. The company refused to pay and was praised for its open, daily updates during the recovery, which cost around 70 million dollars.
daily.why_it_matters: A model for how to respond openly to a ransomware attack.

daily.headline: Five free security steps for small businesses
daily.technical: Back up important data, protect devices from malware, keep phones and laptops updated, use strong passwords with 2-step verification, and teach staff to spot phishing. The NCSC's free Small Business Guide covers each one in plain English.
daily.why_it_matters: Most attacks on small firms are opportunistic and blocked by the basics.
